paper.title: KG-RAG: Enhancing GUI Agent Decision-Making via Knowledge Graph-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation
paper.central_claim: Converting incomplete UI Transition Graphs into a vector database of intent->trajectory pairs through offline intent-guided LLM search (VLM intents, LLM milestones, LLM-scored BFS) and retrieving them online by instruction similarity raises GUI-agent success, decision accuracy and step efficiency (75.8% SR, +8.9 over AutoDroid), works as a plug-and-play module for MobileAgent-v2/UI-TARS, and transfers across OS, devices and to web/desktop.
paper.claim_scope: Per-app knowledge bases built by automated exploration of the same apps that are evaluated (DroidTask English apps; 30 Chinese apps; HarmonyOS); small per-cell task counts; also contributes two author-built benchmarks.

evidence.quote: We introduce KG-RAG, a Knowledge Graph-driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework that transforms fragmented UTGs into structured vector databases for efficient real-time retrieval.
evidence.support_explanation: Central method statement.

evidence.quote: achieving a 75.8% success rate (8.9% improvement over AutoDroid), 84.6% decision accuracy (8.1% improvement), and reducing average task steps from 4.5 to 4.1
evidence.support_explanation: Headline results; 'improvement' is absolute percentage points (66.94 -> 75.80, E015).

evidence.quote: KG-RAG transfers to web/desktop (+40% SR on Weibo-web; +20% on QQ Music-desktop)
evidence.support_explanation: Transfer claim in the abstract.

evidence.quote: we utilize a vision-language model (VLM) to automatically infer these user intents from visual context.

The paper never states how task success or decision accuracy is verified (no checker, human grading or judge model) and defines no ground-truth path for scoring.
No leakage, overlap or held-out analysis between the knowledge-base intents/paths and the evaluation tasks, and no unseen-app evaluation, appears anywhere.
No repeated runs, seeds, standard deviations or confidence intervals are reported.
No LLM-token cost, API cost, online latency or database-size figure is reported for the offline search or the online retrieval.

The only ablation (Tables 7-8) varies the VLM/LLM used for construction and the embedding model; no ablation removes intent generation, milestone scoring, BFS, summarization or retrieval, and no simple baseline (raw UTG in context, shortest path, workflow memory) exists.

signatures.object: Per-app navigation knowledge store built offline from an automated-testing UTG
signatures.information: Offline builder sees UTG screenshots and widgets from authors' xTester exploration (1 h or 8 h per app); VLM sees screens to propose intents; LLM sees intents/trajectories; no real user tasks.
signatures.operation: VLM infers intents -> LLM decomposes into milestones -> LLM predicts milestone-completion probabilities (softmax over logits) and a proximity score -> batched BFS with pruning below a progress threshold -> summarize top trajectories.
signatures.output: Key-value pairs: intent embedding -> action trajectory.
signatures.conditions: UTG must cover the pages containing the task goal; intents must resemble later user instructions; app UI must not drift.
signatures.feedback: LLM scores of paths; no execution replay of stored trajectories.
signatures.selection_rule_data: Progress score primary, proximity tie-break, minimum-progress threshold; selection model choice compared in Table 7 on the evaluation benchmark.
signatures.later_use: Top-K retrieval by cosine between the task instruction embedding and stored intents; retrieved trajectory placed in the agent context.
signatures.failure_boundary: Construction takes hours per app (E031); per-app DBs (E032); gains on UI-TARS SR nil on QQ Music (E019, E020); staleness and wrong-path risk unmeasured.

signatures.information: Retrieved trajectory text as 'proven navigation path'; agent keeps its own perception and decision model (MobileAgent-v2, UI-TARS).
signatures.operation: Insert the top-K retrieved trajectories into the agent prompt/context; no architecture change.
signatures.output: Next action decisions guided by the stored path.
signatures.conditions: Nearest stored intent must actually match the task and the app UI.
signatures.feedback: None specified when retrieval is wrong.
signatures.claimed_effect: MobileAgent-v2 +10-20 SR points, UI-TARS DA +10 on QQ Music (E019-E022); HarmonyOS UI-TARS 61.4->70.9 (E024, E025).
signatures.failure_boundary: No handling of retrieval errors or app drift described.

signatures.information: Authors define tasks with 'intent-action mappings' on 30 + 15 apps; reference sequences are stated to be generated by KG-RAG.
signatures.operation: Construct tasks and reference action sequences; run agents on Android and HarmonyOS devices.
signatures.selection_rule_data: how tasks were chosen/validated not described
signatures.failure_boundary: Task counts inconsistent (300 vs >200); reference path shares a source with the method; scoring procedure not described.

retention_trace.reason: system_method with a persisted knowledge store but no self-improvement loop. The chain is traced; it cannot support a 'retained improvement' conclusion because later tasks are drawn from the same apps and overlap with stored intents is not analysed.

chain.proposed_change: intent->trajectory entries from VLM intents + LLM-scored BFS over the UTG (E006-E010)
chain.selection_data_rule: LLM milestone-progress score with threshold and tie-break; model choices compared on the evaluation benchmark (E008, E009, E029)
chain.later_tasks: instructions in the same apps (DroidTask 162 tasks; KG-Android-Bench; KG-Harmony-Bench)
chain.measured_gain: SR +8.9 (GPT-4, DroidTask), +7.7 (Qwen2-VL-72B); smaller or no SR gain on UI-TARS (E015, E016, E019, E020)

gap.author_gap: Agents lack app-specific knowledge for deeply nested or unconventional navigation; UTGs exist but are low-quality and poorly integrated (Sec 1).
gap.checked_gap: Real and well-illustrated (Figure 1 privacy-policy path). Nearest neighbors: AutoDroid (UTG + LLM planning; named), AWM (workflow induction from experience) and SkillWeaver (exploration-derived skills) in the fixed set; the paper does not discuss or compare the last two. The statement that AutoDroid 'does not fully leverage the UTG' is not turned into a measured failure case; no retrieval-vs-no-retrieval baseline built on the same graph is given.

lineage_closest_adjacent.source: AutoDroid (named by the paper; not in fixed set)
lineage_closest_adjacent.solved: offline UTG + online LLM planning on DroidTask
lineage_closest_adjacent.unsolved_for_this_setting: claimed: rapid retrieval over a structured KG (E033)

lineage_closest_adjacent.solved: induces reusable workflows from experiences and conditions later steps
lineage_closest_adjacent.unsolved_for_this_setting: offline source differs: agent trajectories vs automated-test UTG

gap.residue: Whether LLM-scored UTG paths retrieved by intent similarity beat simply giving the agent the UTG, a shortest path to an LLM-chosen target page, or a workflow memory; whether the DB remains valid after app updates.
gap.stakes: Mobile task efficiency and success on deep-navigation tasks in commercial Chinese apps.
gap.method_response: Precompute navigation paths per intent offline and retrieve them at run time, shifting search from online exploration to an offline LLM-guided graph search.
gap.remaining_gap: No component isolation, no leakage analysis, evaluation on the same apps, benchmark references produced by the method, tiny per-cell n, staleness and cost untreated.
gap.unresolved: Which sub-step (intent generation, milestone scoring, BFS, retrieval) carries the gain.

claims.text: KG-RAG outperforms AutoDroid on DroidTask (GPT-4: SR 66.94->75.80, DA 76.53->84.55, AS 4.49->4.10; Qwen2-VL-72B SR 62.8->70.5).
claims.setting: 12 English apps, 162 tasks, UTG from 1 h xTester
claims.selection_vs_test: DB built from the evaluated apps; no held-out apps
claims.result_denominator: averages of per-app percentages; cells based on 5-16 tasks (E017); single run
claims.allowed_conclusion: Under the authors' setup, KG-RAG scores 7-9 points above AutoDroid on average; whether the UTG used by AutoDroid is equivalent is not stated.

claims.text: KG-RAG is a plug-and-play module for MobileAgent-v2 and UI-TARS.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Positive shifts in most cells, strongest for the weaker agent; for UI-TARS on QQ Music success rate does not change.

claims.text: KG-RAG generalizes across devices/OS and to web/desktop without retraining.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Same-app cross-platform improvements on tiny cells; not evidence for unseen apps.

claims.text: UTG extraction accuracy saturates at about 4 hours per complex app.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A saturation point observed on one app and 10 tasks.

claims.text: Intent-guided LLM search is what produces the improvements.
claims.selection_vs_test: Table 7 compares variants on the evaluation benchmark
claims.allowed_conclusion: Only that construction-model and embedding choice matter (SR 67.00-78.33).

claims.text: KG-Android-Bench/KG-Harmony-Bench are comprehensive benchmarks (300 tasks, 30 apps; 150 tasks, 15 apps).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Task lists exist; validity of references/scoring is unstated and references derive from the method.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On DroidTask's 12 English apps with a 1-hour xTester UTG, adding the compiled intent-trajectory store raises GPT-4 average SR from 66.94 to 75.80 (Qwen2-VL-72B 62.8 to 70.5) relative to AutoDroid in single-run per-app averages; plug-in and cross-platform results are directionally positive on 10-task cells for the same apps.
unresolved: leakage between stored intents/paths and evaluation tasks, including benchmark reference paths generated by KG-RAG
component isolation (intents, milestones, BFS, retrieval) and simple baselines
assessment.reproduction_note: All numbers are author-reported; no code was run.
assessment.evidence_level_note: 'online' only: memory built from the evaluated apps caps transfer (EVIDENCE rule 2); web/desktop gains are on the same app family with 10-task cells.

G.reason: A real, illustrated bottleneck (deep navigation in unfamiliar apps) with AutoDroid as the explicit neighbor, but AWM/SkillWeaver-type neighbors are not discussed or compared and the claimed AutoDroid shortcoming is not shown as a measured failure.

M.reason: Concrete offline-to-online mechanism whose logic is understandable, but key assumptions are untested: VLM-inferred intents match real instructions, LLM milestone scores identify correct paths, and nothing distinguishes the design from simply exposing the UTG or a shortest path.

X.reason: Pipeline stages, scoring and storage are described and costs of construction are given; K, thresholds, prompts and integration with each agent are not, verification of retrieved paths is absent, and staleness/failure boundaries are limited to cost.

E.measurement.reason: Online runs on real devices, but the scoring procedure for SR/DA is not described, the new benchmark's reference paths are generated by the method itself, task counts disagree (300 vs >200), and the LLM path scorer is unvalidated.

E.causality.reason: With/without comparisons exist for several agents, but there is no ablation of any KG-RAG sub-step, no raw-UTG/shortest-path/workflow-memory baseline, and the AutoDroid comparison does not establish that both use the same graph.

E.holdout.reason: Knowledge is built from the same apps used for evaluation; no overlap/leak analysis or unseen apps; transfer rows are the same app families with 10-task cells; benchmark references are produced by KG-RAG.

E.statistics.reason: Single reported numbers with per-cell n of about 5-16 (DroidTask) or 10 (QQ Music, Weibo), no repeats or CI, averages of per-app percentages, and one DA decrease (File Manager).

E.cost.reason: Construction time (1 h / 8 h) and a time-vs-quality table are reported and average steps are given, but LLM token cost for the search, retrieval latency, DB size and K are absent.

status.reason: Full html text read including limitations; algorithm bodies/figures are not in the text but the method is described in prose and the experimental tables are complete.

rationale.summary: KG-RAG compiles an automated-testing UI transition graph into a per-app vector store of intent-to-trajectory pairs using VLM-proposed intents, LLM-scored milestone BFS and summaries, and retrieves them by instruction similarity at run time. Averages over DroidTask apps favour KG-RAG against AutoDroid (66.94 -> 75.80 SR), and plug-in and cross-platform tables are mostly positive, but all evidence is on the apps the knowledge was built from, with 5-16 task cells, no component ablations, undescribed scoring and benchmark references derived from the method itself.
strengths: Practical offline/online split with explicit construction-cost reporting (Table 11)
Multiple agents, backends, devices and OS tested
Clear motivating example and mechanism description
weaknesses: Held-out apps and leakage analysis absent; reference paths produced by KG-RAG
No ablation of the search/intent/milestone components or simple baselines (raw UTG, shortest path, workflow memory)
Scoring protocol undefined, task counts inconsistent, tiny n, no repeats
UI-TARS success rate unchanged on its one detailed table
